analysis.investment_thesis: Identixweb is a tiny Rs 90 Cr Shopify-app shop with decent ROCE (34.3%) but revenue of just Rs 9 Cr — too small, too undifferentiated, and dependent on a single third-party ecosystem (Shopify) to warrant serious capital. Invert: a sub-scale services firm riding someone else's platform is precisely the fragile setup I avoid.
key_strengths: High reported ROCE 34.3% / ROE 24.8% on small base
Zero debt; equity-funded with Rs 21 Cr reserves post-IPO
Operating cash flow positive 3/3 years; revenue grew 50% in FY25
key_risks: Platform dependency — Shopify ecosystem controls its fate entirely
Sub-Rs 10 Cr revenue = no moat, no scale, likely customer concentration
FCF negative last 2 years (-4, -2); IPO cash deployed without a track record
red_flags: Assets tripled to Rs 35 Cr in FY25 via IPO — capital raised faster than proven deployment capability
Net profit flat at Rs 3 Cr despite revenue growth; Rs 1 Cr other income in FY24 flattered earnings
Effective P/E on post-money equity base is closer to 30x, not 18.6x
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The ratios look attractive in isolation — 34% ROCE, no debt, 63% promoter holding — but these are artifacts of a tiny denominator. A company doing Rs 9 Cr of revenue building Shopify apps has no durable competitive advantage; Shopify itself, App Store policy changes, or any of thousands of competing agencies can erase the business overnight. This is exactly the single-ecosystem dependency I invert against: you don't own the distribution, the customer, or the platform rules.

The balance sheet inflation is the tell. Assets went from Rs 12 Cr to Rs 35 Cr in one year, reserves from Rs 3 Cr to Rs 21 Cr — fresh IPO cash now sitting idle while FCF is negative. Market cap of Rs 90 Cr against Rs 3 Cr net profit on a fragile services model is not cheap. Pass. Come back when there's Rs 100+ Cr of revenue with proven product IP independent of Shopify.
